title: Reliable Agent Workflow Capstone
summary: This intermediate module enables you to design and evaluate a provider-neutral agent workflow that records observations, validates results, and stops safely. After completing it, you can turn an underspecified workflow into one with explicit success criteria, evidence requirements, and failure handling.
objectives: Define a task contract containing a goal, permitted actions, success criteria, and stopping conditions.
Separate a proposed action from the observation returned after that action.
Add validation and safe failure handling to an agent workflow.
Evaluate a workflow trace and decide whether its final result is supported by recorded evidence.

sections.title: What changed in this update
paragraphs: The changed citation was content/modules/reliable-agent-workflows/reliable-agent-capstone.json. It was a local repository path, was listed with an unregistered publisher, and had never been verified as a public source.

That citation has been replaced by the canonical public paper URL listed in the sources field. The change affects the module's source provenance and the support for its explanation of workflows that alternate reasoning, actions, and observations.
sections.callout: The correction is limited to the invalid citation and the material directly affected by its provenance.

sections.title: Intermediate scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that you can read a structured task description, distinguish generated output from externally returned information, and recognize a basic validation rule.
It does not assume knowledge of any named provider, software product, configuration system, or programming language. The workflow is described with provider-neutral concepts.

sections.title: Define the task contract
paragraphs: Begin with a task contract. State the goal, the inputs that may be used, the actions that are permitted, the evidence required for success, and the conditions that require the workflow to stop.

A goal alone is not enough. For example, produce an answer describes an output but does not say how to determine whether the answer is supported. A stronger contract requires each material conclusion to be linked to a recorded observation and requires a final validation step before completion.

Stopping conditions should cover both success and failure. Success occurs only when the stated validation rules pass. Failure handling should stop or request human review when required evidence is missing, an action repeatedly fails, or the workflow reaches its allowed boundary without satisfying the contract.

sections.title: Keep actions and observations separate
paragraphs: An action is a proposed operation. An observation is information returned after that operation. Treating the proposed action as though it were a completed result creates unsupported conclusions.

For each cycle, record the current objective, the selected action, the resulting observation, and the next decision. The cited paper describes an approach that interleaves reasoning traces with task-specific actions. In this module, that separation is used to make the trace reviewable.
Only recorded observations should be used as evidence. If an expected observation is absent, the workflow should not invent it or silently treat the action as successful.

sections.title: Validate and recover safely
paragraphs: Validation compares the accumulated evidence with the task contract. A validator should check whether required fields are present, whether conclusions are supported by observations, and whether every success condition has been met.

A failed validation is information, not permission to claim success. The workflow may take another permitted action when that action can address the failure. Otherwise, it should stop safely and report what is missing.

Retries should respond to a specific failure. Repeating the same action without new information does not resolve an unsupported conclusion. The trace should retain the failed attempt so that a reviewer can see why the workflow continued or stopped.

sections.title: Evaluate the completed workflow
paragraphs: Evaluate a workflow by reading its trace from the task contract to the final decision. Confirm that every action was permitted, every claimed result is backed by an observation, validation occurred before completion, and unresolved failures were disclosed.

A reliable completion has four visible properties: the success criteria are explicit, actions and observations remain distinct, the final validator passes, and the evidence supports the final result. If any property is absent, the workflow should not report successful completion.

You can now improve a workflow that merely produces an answer by adding a task contract, an action-observation trace, validation rules, and safe stopping behavior. These additions let you explain why the final result should be accepted or why the workflow stopped without one.

questions.prompt: What did the currency update change?
choices: It replaced an unverified local-path citation with the canonical public paper URL, affecting source provenance and support for the action-observation explanation.
It added a named software product and its configuration keys.
It changed the module from intermediate to beginner.
It removed the requirement to validate a result.
questions.explanation: The update section states that the prior citation was an unverified local repository path and that it was replaced by the canonical public paper URL.

questions.prompt: Which item may be used as evidence for a workflow conclusion?
choices: A proposed action that has not run
A recorded observation returned after an action
An expected result that was never observed
A repeated assertion in the final answer
questions.explanation: The module states that only recorded observations should be used as evidence. A proposed or expected result is not an observation.

questions.prompt: What should happen when final validation fails and no permitted action can address the failure?
choices: The workflow should report success because it attempted the task.
The workflow should remove the failed attempt from its trace.
The workflow should stop safely and report what is missing.
The workflow should treat the proposed action as a successful observation.
questions.explanation: The validation section says that when no permitted action can address a failed validation, the workflow should stop safely and disclose the missing information.

questions.prompt: Which condition is required before the workflow reports successful completion?
choices: The final validator passes and the evidence supports the result.
At least one action was proposed.
The trace contains no failed attempts.
questions.explanation: The capstone evaluation requires a passing final validator and evidence supporting the final result. Failed attempts may remain in the trace.
